messages.subject: Simulation of regression parameters
parts:
I have a model:
#Random intercept
form2 = y ~ -1 + intercept + z +
  f(idx, model="dmatern", locations = loc,
    hyper = list(range = list(initial = log(range),
                              param = c(range, 0.5))))

fit_p=inla(form2,
           data = data_df_pois,
           family = "poisson",
           #control.predictor = list(compute=TRUE, link=1),
           control.compute = list(dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE, config = TRUE),
           #control.fixed = list(prec = 1),
           control.inla=list(strategy="laplace",int.strategy="ccd"),
           verbose=TRUE,debug=TRUE,safe=FALSE,
           num.threads = 2) #number of CPU threads that INLA can run in parallel

summary(fit_p)
And I want to simulate the parameters. If I use:
N <- nrow(data_df_pois)  # Sample size
# Simulation of 10000 sets of regression parameters
SimData <- inla.posterior.sample(n = 10000, fit_p)
Npar <- nrow(fit_p$summary.fixed)              
# Extract regression parameters
vars <- rownames(fit_p$summary.fixed)
Betas_sim <- inla.posterior.sample.eval( vars  , SimData) does the Betas_sim  contain simulations for the random intercept or only the fixed part of the intercept?

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Simulation of regression parameters
parts:
Hi,

it might help if you referred to your model components by name instead of what your interpretation of them are.
The "intercept" component is a single scalar value (assuming your data has 1 in the "intercept" variable).
The "z" component is a regular "fixed effect" covariate, i.e. some beta * z.
Your idx model component is spatially varying.
In R-INLA, "intercept" and "z" are "fixed" effects, and "idx" is a "random" effect.

Which of the three is it that you're looking for?
Or is it that you want the model to have an additional iid effect for each location? Then you have to add that explicitly.
The term "random intercept" can only be interpreted in the context of the precise interpretation of a specific model and could potentially mean several different things, so you need to make it clear precisely what model you have, and/or what model you want to have, in a way that isn't relying on arbitrary terminology.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Simulation of regression parameters
parts:
I see.
The dmatern component output summary should be visible in $summary.random, and SimData should contain samples of all the model components.
Your “vars” names only looks at summary.fixed, so will miss all of the random effects in the model even if they’re actually in SimData.
Add names(fit_p$summary.random) to the vars vector and you should get what you’re looking for.
Finn

Στις Δευτέρα 7 Απριλίου 2025 στις 6:04:05 μ.μ. UTC+2, ο χρήστης Finn Lindgren έγραψε:
Hi,

it might help if you referred to your model components by name instead of what your interpretation of them are.
The "intercept" component is a single scalar value (assuming your data has 1 in the "intercept" variable).
The "z" component is a regular "fixed effect" covariate, i.e. some beta * z.
Your idx model component is spatially varying.
In R-INLA, "intercept" and "z" are "fixed" effects, and "idx" is a "random" effect.

Which of the three is it that you're looking for?
Or is it that you want the model to have an additional iid effect for each location? Then you have to add that explicitly.
The term "random intercept" can only be interpreted in the context of the precise interpretation of a specific model and could potentially mean several different things, so you need to make it clear precisely what model you have, and/or what model you want to have, in a way that isn't relying on arbitrary terminology.

Finn
